items.prompt: What are the three ways to obtain crocodilians recognized by CITES and the Crocodile Specialist Group?

options.label: Hunting, trapping, and fishing
options.feedback: Hunting, trapping, and fishing are methods for taking wild animals, but they are not the three recognized ways for obtaining crocodilians. The recognized ways are ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding.

options.label: Farming, poaching, and tourism
options.feedback: Poaching is illegal and not a recognized method, and tourism is a way facilities earn extra money, not a way to obtain crocodilians. The correct recognized categories are ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding.

options.label: Ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding
options.feedback: That's correct. These three categories are the ways recognized by CITES and the Crocodile Specialist Group for obtaining crocodilians.

options.label: Egg collection, juvenile release, and skinning
options.feedback: Egg collection and skinning are steps within farming or ranching, and juvenile release is a conservation action, but none of these are the recognized categories for obtaining crocodilians. The correct ones are ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding.

items.ok_line: Ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding are the official ways.
items.ko_line: Those are not the three categories CITES and the CSG use.
items.exp_text: The three ways to obtain crocodilians are ranching, wild harvesting, and captive breeding. Ranching means incubating and rearing hatchlings collected from the wild, while captive breeding keeps adult breeders to produce eggs on site, and wild harvesting refers to taking eggs or animals from nature.

items.prompt: What is the main difference between an alligator farm and an alligator ranch?

options.label: Farms only collect eggs from the wild, while ranches keep breeding adults
options.feedback: That is the opposite of the actual difference. Farms keep breeding adults in their facilities, while ranches only collect hatchlings from the wild and rear them. So this statement is reversed.

options.label: Farms keep breeding adults to produce their own eggs, while ranches incubate and rear hatchlings collected from the wild
options.feedback: Correct. That is the core difference: farms breed their own animals, ranches rear wild-collected hatchlings without keeping breeding adults.

options.label: Farms are only for tourism, while ranches are only for meat
options.feedback: This mixes up purpose with method. Both farms and ranches can produce meat or skins, and farms or ranches may add tourism for extra income, but the real difference is about whether breeding adults are kept on site.

options.label: Ranches are open to the public, while farms are closed
options.feedback: This is not the difference. Both farms and ranches can be open or closed to visitors; the defining difference is that farms breed their own alligators, while ranches rear wild-collected hatchlings.

items.ok_line: A farm keeps breeding adults; a ranch only rears wild hatchlings.
items.ko_line: The difference is not about tourism or eggs alone.
items.exp_text: An alligator farm keeps breeding adults in its facilities to produce its own eggs, though it may also collect eggs from the wild. A ranch does not keep breeding adults; it incubates and rears hatchlings that were collected from the wild. That is the key difference.

items.prompt: What does an open-cycle crocodilian operation focus on?

options.label: Harvesting as many animals as possible
options.feedback: That describes a closed-cycle operation, which is primarily concerned with harvest. An open-cycle operation is concerned with the health of the wild population, not just maximizing harvest.

options.label: Keeping all adult females in captivity
options.feedback: That is a feature of closed-cycle operations, where adult females are kept in captivity to lay eggs for harvest. Open-cycle operations focus on supporting wild populations.

options.label: Making the highest profit for the owners
options.feedback: Profit is the main concern of closed-cycle operations, not open-cycle ones. Open-cycle operations aim for the overall health of the species, even though costs may be similar.

options.label: The health of the wild population
options.feedback: Correct. Open-cycle programs use captive rearing to supplement wild populations, so their main goal is the well-being of the species in the wild.

items.ok_line: It aims for the health of the wild population.
items.ko_line: Profit and harvest belong to closed-cycle operations.
items.exp_text: Open-cycle operations are concerned with the health of the wild population. They use captive rearing as a way to supplement or support wild numbers, rather than aiming primarily at harvest or profit.

items.prompt: Which disease is caused by a Parapoxvirus and affects hatchlings and juveniles?

options.label: Caiman pox
options.feedback: Caiman pox is caused by a different virus and causes white lesions, but the disease caused by Parapoxvirus is crocodile pox, and it causes a brown residue.

options.label: Crocodile pox
options.feedback: Correct. Crocodile pox is caused by Parapoxvirus and affects hatchlings and juveniles, causing a brown residue around the eyes, oral cavity, and tail.

options.label: Mycoplasmosis
options.feedback: Mycoplasmosis causes polyarthritis and pneumonia, not a skin disease with a brown residue. It is not caused by Parapoxvirus.

options.label: Adenoviral hepatitis
options.feedback: Adenoviral hepatitis causes organ failure and death, not the skin residue seen in crocodile pox. It is not caused by Parapoxvirus.

items.ok_line: Parapoxvirus causes crocodile pox in young crocodilians.
items.ko_line: The virus and symptoms point only to crocodile pox.
items.exp_text: Crocodile pox is caused by Parapoxvirus and affects hatchlings and juveniles. It produces a brown residue around the eyes, oral cavity, and tail. Caiman pox, in contrast, is a separate disease with white lesions.
